evidence.observation: Datasource-URL normalization that runs before indexing: SSH (`git@host:path.git`, optional `ssh://`), HTTPS (`https://host/path.git`) and already-normalized bare `host/path` inputs are all collapsed to the same `host/path` form with the `.git` suffix stripped. This is what makes re-indexing the same repository idempotent regardless of how the remote URL was spelled.

Builds the stable per-datasource index key as `${normalizeRepoUrl(repo)}:${branch || "main"}`. Because it reuses normalizeRepoUrl, the three URL spellings above produce one identical key, which is the unique ownership/idempotency key for the datasource bucket.

Frontmatter fence regex `/^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---?
?/`, tolerant of CRLF line endings. It defines exactly the block that a pre-index normalizer must canonicalize (BOM/CRLF stripped, fence required).

Tolerant frontmatter reader: it splits page content into `frontmatter` + `body`, but a missing block or a YAML parse failure is swallowed and degraded to `{ type: "other" }` with `hasFrontmatter: false`; a non-object or blank `type` is also coerced to "other". This is precisely the gap the task closes — tolerant read must be paired with a strict normalization/validation gate that rejects malformed metadata before the page enters the index.

Canonical page writer used for producing/rewriting pages: fixed field order (type -> title -> description -> sources -> tags -> timestamp -> other custom fields), `type` defaults to "other", the body is trimmed, and `locked` is deliberately never emitted. A normalize-before-index step should re-emit through this same shape so the stored page is canonical.

Ingest-side normalization of a candidate page's `sources`: it filters non-string entries and force-adds the current source filename, rebuilding the page through buildPage. Shows that per-page metadata normalization already happens between extraction and commit — the natural insertion point for a strict reject-malformed-metadata gate.

Normalizes a candidate page's on-disk path before commit: it reads `type`/`title` from frontmatter, trims them, slugifies the title and maps type -> directory (`entity` -> `entities`), falling back to a directory-normalized version of the LLM path. Demonstrates the pre-index normalization contract that the demo's `normalizeAndIndexEntry` reproduces.

claims.claim: Before indexing, datasource identity is normalized: normalizeRepoUrl collapses SSH, HTTPS and bare git URLs to one `host/path` form (stripping `.git`), and sourceKey composes that with the branch (defaulting to `main`) into a single stable index key, so the same repository cannot be indexed into two buckets.

The existing frontmatter reader is deliberately tolerant, not rejecting: parseFrontmatter downgrades a missing fence, malformed YAML, a non-object payload, or a blank `type` to `{ type: "other" }` (hasFrontmatter false for the failure cases), so malformed metadata would be silently indexed unless a strict normalization/validation gate rejects it first.

The canonical normalized page shape is defined by buildPage: fixed field order, trimmed body, `type` required with "other" fallback, and `locked` never written — so a normalize-before-index step must re-emit page content through this shape (and must drop `locked`) to stay consistent with rewrite/merge paths.

Normalization already sits immediately before commit in the ingest pipeline — ensureSources coerces `sources` to strings and force-adds the current source, while canonicalizePagePath derives the canonical `wiki/<dir>/<slug>.md` path from normalized type/title — which is the correct insertion point for failing closed on malformed metadata before any page is written.

The delivered executable demo puts that contract into practice: it normalizes repo URLs and markdown/frontmatter (BOM/CRLF, type trim, scalar->list coercion, de-duplication, dropped `locked`, canonical field order) and rejects malformed metadata with typed codes (EMPTY_REPO_URL, MISSING_FRONTMATTER, MALFORMED_YAML, INVALID_TYPE, INVALID_FIELD); the recorded run passes all 10 contract cases.

conclusion: TencentDB Agent Memory already has both halves of the normalization contract for indexing — normalizeRepoUrl/sourceKey give every datasource a single idempotent key, and buildPage defines the canonical page shape (fixed field order, trimmed body, `locked` never written) — but parseFrontmatter intentionally fails open, degrading missing or malformed frontmatter to `{ type: "other" }`. Normalizing markdown/frontmatter before indexing therefore requires wrapping the tolerant reader in a strict gate: canonicalize BOM/CRLF/fence and type/title/sources/tags (coercing scalar values to de-duplicated string lists, dropping `locked`, preserving unknown fields), and reject malformed metadata with descriptive typed codes (EMPTY_REPO_URL, MISSING_FRONTMATTER, MALFORMED_YAML, INVALID_TYPE, INVALID_FIELD) so no degraded page is ever indexed. The dependency-free demo .prale-eval/demo/normalize-and-validate.mjs implements exactly this and its recorded run passes 10/10 cases.
